item.title: In 1868, an eclipse in India revealed an element found on Earth 27 years later
item.description: During the solar eclipse of 1868 in India, astronomers stumbled upon an enigmatic yellow spectral line, initially observed by Pierre Jules Janssen. Although its significance was not immediately recognized, Norman Lockyer soon named the unidentified element helium upon further analysis. Eventually, William Ramsay verified helium's presence on Earth in 1895 by extracting it from a mineral, solidifying Janssen's pioneering approach to studying solar prominences.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Red Handfish, the endangered 'walking' fish that became Photo Ark's 18,000th species
item.description: For 20 years, photographer Joel Sartore has been documenting animals through his Photo Ark project, which has now reached its 18,000th species. The latest addition is the critically endangered red handfish, a tiny marine fish that uses its fins to move across the seafloor. Sartore hopes the project will raise awareness about threatened species and help preserve a record of animals that could disappear.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Discarded salon hair is being transformed into an oil-absorbing barrier that protects mangroves from oil spills in Rio de Janeiro
item.description: Discarded human hair is now preventing oil pollution in Rio de Janeiro's Guanabara Bay. Each gram of hair absorbs approximately five grams of oil, repelling water effectively. These hair barriers, made from salon waste, can remain in the water for four months. The initiative protects vulnerable mangrove ecosystems from chronic and everyday oil leaks. This innovative project aims to aid the recovery of the bay's marine life.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: The Netherlands built new islands from 37 million tonnes of lake sediment
item.description: In an innovative move, Dutch engineers have fashioned new islands from lake sediment to rejuvenate a fragile freshwater ecosystem. These manmade structures have swiftly drawn an array of flora and fauna, notably various bird populations. The initiative has revitalised an ailing lake, transforming it into a bustling habitat for marine life and migratory birds alike.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: California’s Shasta Dam flooded Kennett, a copper-mining town beneath Lake Shasta
item.description: Once a bustling northern California mining hub, Kennett was swallowed by the depths of Shasta Lake following the construction of the Shasta Dam. This ambitious federal project aimed at water management inundated the town, which thrived on copper mining and railroads. Today, only historical accounts and the lake itself hint at the vibrant community that once existed in this submerged landscape.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Doc Revisits EDP445 Controversy: film tracks rise, sting and new claims; proceeds go to RAINN
item.description: EDP445, whose real name is Bryant Moreland, is back in focus through Mike Clum’s documentaryThe Sick Mind of EDP445. The film revisits the 2021 sting that ended his YouTube career and includes Moreland’s claim that God saved him from arrest during another alleged incident. It also introduces his girlfriend, Marissa, and discusses their relationship.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: Knowles Rejects Debate Role: commentator refuses Kirk murder clash; urges trial over podcasts
item.description: Candace Owens is facing renewed scrutiny after Michael Knowles refused to moderate a proposed debate between Owens and Andrew Wilson over Charlie Kirk’s murder. Knowles said he believes the evidence points to Tyler Robinson and argued that guilt should be determined in court rather than through podcasts. He also criticized the growing industry of Charlie Kirk murder content, while acknowledging that Owens’ series has attracted significant attention and views.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Brother’s Message Fuels Rumors: Reddit plea urges prayers, rejects gossip
item.description: Dalton Ain’t Worried and Sako have not confirmed a breakup. Comments believed to be from Dalton’s brother Christopher Adkison say the couple is going through a difficult time and ask people to stop spreading rumors. Dalton’s emotional video and unverified arrest reports have raised questions, but there is still no confirmed evidence that the couple has separated.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: Teen Recounts Violent Joke: Jane details online exchanges with D4vd; case stays unproven in court
item.description: D4vd faces renewed scrutiny after a former teenage online friend recalled an alleged joke in which he referenced cutting off her arms. She said the comment seemed harmless at the time but became disturbing after details from Celeste Rivas Hernandez’s autopsy emerged. D4vd has pleaded not guilty and will stand trial for murder and other charges. The teen stressed that her account does not prove wrongdoing or connect the alleged joke to Rivas Hernandez’s death.

item.title: Nasa's New Horizons reached Arrokoth in 2019, revealing the early solar system
item.description: NASA's New Horizons spacecraft made an astonishing visit to Arrokoth, a remote Kuiper Belt object, uncovering vital clues about the solar system's early formation. This ancient body exhibits a fascinating two-lobed structure, hinting at a gentle collision between two distinct entities. Furthermore, its strikingly red surface is indicative of complex organic materials, giving scientists a rare window into our cosmic origins.

item.title: Trump Media Q2 results: US president led media ventrue posts $238 million loss as crypto holdings tumble
item.description: In the second quarter, Trump Media faced a dramatic loss of $238 million despite seeing its revenue more than double. However, operating losses expanded significantly, prompting the company to abandon new ventures like online betting and cryptocurrency. Their focus has shifted to the Truth API service, aimed at trading firms, while a nuclear fusion project with TAE Technologies remains on track.
